candidates.explanation: I couldn't see this function's body, so this is inferred from the symbol locations and the bug report. refreshToken takes the sessionId and hash from the refresh JWT and issues a new token pair. A refresh token can only be rotated safely if two things happen. The stored session hash must be compared with the hash in the presented token. The session must then be updated with a newly generated hash, and that same new hash must go into the new tokens. The replay symptom points to one of these steps being missing or wrong. Either the incoming hash isn't checked against session.hash, or the session isn't saved with the new hash before tokens are issued. It may also be that the new tokens are signed with the old hash. In that case the old refresh token stays valid and can be replayed.

This function signs the refresh token with the session hash it is given. If refreshToken passes it the old session hash instead of a freshly generated one, the new refresh token carries the same hash as the old one. The old token then still matches the session and can be replayed.

This only validates the JWT payload (it checks that sessionId is present). It doesn't check the session hash against the database, so it can't reject a rotated token. The check has to happen in AuthService.refreshToken. This is a lower-probability candidate.

fix.description: In AuthService.refreshToken, load the session by data.sessionId and throw UnauthorizedException if it's missing or session.hash !== data.hash. Then generate a new random hash (for example crypto.createHash('sha256').update(randomStringGenerator()).digest('hex')). Persist it with sessionService.update(session.id, { hash }) and await that call. Finally call getTokensData with the new hash, not the old one, so the previous refresh token no longer matches the stored hash and is rejected. I couldn't read the function body, so check which of these steps is missing.
